reply_text:
I found four dated predictions from Jensen Huang in 2017. All of them are about self-driving cars, and none is about AGI. The Audi "on the road by 2020" claim you already have shows up only as the blogger's paraphrase on Nvidia's live blog, so it adds no new quote.

- **CES keynote, 4 January (transcript):** he said deep learning made it possible to "imagine realizing this vision in the next year". The vision was the car as "your most personal robot". This is a separate claim from the recorded Audi one. The Singju Post page I opened seems to hold only the first part of the transcript and doesn't include the Audi section.
- **Earnings call, August (news report only):** he gave a timeline: robot taxis in commercial service "starting 2019", and fully autonomous branded cars around 2020–2021. I saw these words only as excerpts in a Motley Fool article dated 20 August. I didn't open the official call transcript, so the exact day of the call isn't confirmed.
- **Taipei, 26 October (news report only):** "It will take no more than 4 years to have fully autonomous cars on the road." This comes from a NextBigFuture repost of a Reuters story.
- **Not quoted:** a VentureBeat report of the 9 November earnings call ("Next year … Year after that, robot taxis …") turned up only in a search snippet. I didn't open it, so it isn't listed as a candidate. It's the best page to open next.

The MIT Technology Review interview from May ("AI is going to eat software") had no date in it. Its "couple of decades" line is about chip performance, so I left it out. The Fortune profile I opened was cut off and had no forecasts in it.
